title: Warm, Yeasty Norwegian Mushroom Skillet
description: A cozy, yeasty dish featuring wood ear mushrooms, perfect for a cold winter evening. This skillet is a twist on traditional Norwegian cuisine, made with macrobiotic-friendly ingredients.
instructions: In a small bowl, combine flour, yeast, and sugar to make the dough starter.
Add the warm milk to the bowl and mix until smooth.
Knead the dough starter for 2-3 minutes until it becomes elastic.
Place the dough starter in a greased bowl, cover it with plastic wrap, and let it rise in a warm place for 1-2 hours, or until doubled in size.
While the dough is rising, heat 2 tablespoons of butter in a 12-inch cast-iron skillet over medium heat.
Add the sliced onion and cook until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute, until fragrant.
Add the wood ear mushrooms and cook until they release their moisture and start to brown, about 5 minutes.
Dust the skillet with flour to prevent the dough from sticking.
Punch down the dough starter and shape it into a round or oblong shape.
Place the dough in the skillet, pressing it gently to fit the shape of the pan.
Cover the skillet with a lid and cook for 10-12 minutes, or until the dough is golden brown and crispy.
Remove the lid and sprinkle the grated cheddar cheese on top of the dough.
Return the skillet to the oven and cook for an additional 2-3 minutes, or until the cheese is melted and bubbly.
Remove the skillet from the oven and let it cool for a few minutes before slicing and serving.
Garnish with chopped parsley, if desired.
